answer: Because the entropy is measured at the voyage gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the mirror audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 64 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the cipher panel. That is 4 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
